commentary: Today, the DCE iron ore futures trended stronger, with the most-traded contract I2609 closing at 787.5 yuan/mt, up 0.90% from the previous trading session. Spot prices rose 6-7 from the previous day. Traders showed moderate enthusiasm in quoƟng, while steel mills maintained a strong wait-and-see aƫtude with fewer inquiries; overall spot transacƟons were thin. Fundamentals: according to the latest SMM survey data, daily average hot metal producƟon pulled back to 2.4405 million mt, down 8,900 mt WoW. Some steel mills have successively formulated short-term maintenance plans, and overall hot metal producƟon has begun to show signs of peaking and pulling back. Nevertheless, as downstream demand and cost support remained relaƟvely solid, iron ore price support remained ﬁrm. AddiƟonally, inﬂuenced by recent policies, market expectaƟons for Ɵghtening liquidity in bulk commodiƟes were strong, with some bullish senƟment emerging in the market overall; however, in the long term, Ɵghtening of iron ore trade liquidity is not sustainable. Therefore, ore prices may conƟnue the ﬂuctuaƟng trend at highs in the short term, without strong unilateral momentum.
